summary: Verified hreflang + canonical + og:locale SEO tags on public shop and product pages (devhub / talk-to-a-developer) for languages en/es/pt/fr/de/nl. All 4 acceptance criteria from the review pass. Wrote pytest regression suite (5 tests, all green).

issues: og:url meta tag still uses broken production host 'https://dynopay.com//shop' (missing handle, double slash). This is OUTSIDE the review's scope (which only asserts canonical + hreflang have no broken host, both of which are correct), but it is a real residual SEO leak on the same app-shell fallback and worth fixing by the main agent. Seen on: shop (bare), shop?lang=fr, and product page (bare + ?lang=de) — pattern is 'dynopay.com//shop' and 'dynopay.com//p'.

acceptance_criteria_results.shop_default_no_lang: PASS — exactly 1 canonical=…/devhub/shop, 7 hreflang alternates (en,es,pt,fr,de,nl,x-default) with correct per-lang URLs, no duplicates, no broken host in any <link> tag, og:locale=en (1 tag).
acceptance_criteria_results.shop_lang_fr: PASS — canonical is self-referential (…/devhub/shop?lang=fr), 7 hreflang alternates correct, og:locale=fr (1 tag), <title> localized to 'The Dev Store — Boutique · Dynopay'.
acceptance_criteria_results.product_lang_de: PASS — canonical self-ref (…/devhub/p/talk-to-a-developer?lang=de), 7 hreflang alternates correct, og:locale=de (1 tag).
acceptance_criteria_results.product_default_regression: PASS — HTTP 200, canonical=bare URL, 7 hreflang cluster present, og:locale=en (1 tag).

action_items: OPTIONAL / out-of-scope: fix og:url meta tag to also override the app-shell fallback — currently emits 'https://dynopay.com//shop' and 'https://dynopay.com//p' (broken host with double slash + stripped handle). Same key-based dedupe pattern that fixed canonical/hreflang should be applied to og:url in pages/[handle]/shop.tsx and pages/[handle]/p/[slug].tsx.
critical_code_review_comments: Attribute is emitted as React camelCase `hrefLang="…"` which serializes to lowercase-preserving-camelcase in the SSR HTML. Any downstream tooling grepping with case-sensitive `hreflang=` will miss the tags — use case-insensitive matching (as done here). Not a bug per se, HTML attributes are case-insensitive, but worth noting for other test/QA scripts.

The app-shell fallback in _app.tsx uses a hardcoded broken 'https://dynopay.com//<path>' base for canonical/hreflang/og. Page-level next/head keys correctly override canonical + hreflang, but og:url is NOT keyed the same way and leaks through — see action item.
seed_data_creation: None — read-only prod DB per instructions.
context_for_next_testing_agent: SEO hreflang/canonical implementation is verified working on shop + product pages. Regression suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_seo_hreflang.py — includes a retry loop for occasional Cloudflare edge 404 flaps. Remaining known issue (out of this review's scope): og:url meta tag still emits the broken 'dynopay.com//<path>' from the _app.tsx fallback because it isn't overridden with a matching next/head key at the page level.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature verified as correctly implemented. Residual og:url leak RCA: pages/_app.tsx emits <meta property="og:url" content="https://dynopay.com//<path>"/> using a broken hardcoded fallback that strips the handle and yields a double slash. pages/[handle]/shop.tsx and pages/[handle]/p/[slug].tsx keyed their canonical + hreflang tags so next/head dedupes and page values win, but og:url was not added to that override list, so the broken app-shell value survives into the final SSR HTML.
